text: Final categorization: OK (Justification: The paper is a non-review research article that explicitly implements national-scale spatial modeling of future land use across the entire Netherlands using the Land Use Scanner model. Its primary objective is to simulate and compare alternative futures of agricultural land use under two contrasting socio-economic scenarios (Global Economy and Regional Community). The study provides quantitative scenario-based projections of land use change up to 2030, including mapped outputs (Figure 2) and quantitative estimates of agricultural area change (Figure 1). The modeling approach is spatially explicit (500 × 500 m grid), includes multiple land-use classes (including four agricultural types), and balances competing land claims based on suitability metrics. All core inclusion criteria are met: national-scale implementation, primary focus on LULC prediction, ≥2 quantitative future scenarios, spatial modeling with mapped outputs, and quantitative change estimates. None of the exclusion criteria apply.)
